eligibility: I can study at a postgraduate level in English
I am a citizen of an African country
I am between the ages of 19 and 29 in the year of applying
By 1 Jan 2028, I will have an undergraduate degree with excellent academic results (above 70% or upper-second class Honours)
I aspire to be an ethical leader and I am committed to using my talents to advance equality, freedom and human dignity in Africa
I admire Nelson Mandela's ability to bridge divides and bring people together around our common humanity
I am prepared to reflect deeply on my own leadership and undergo a process of personal change and growth
existing.eligibility_summary: Citizen of an African country, aged 19 to 29 in the year of applying, with an undergraduate degree completed by 1 January 2028 with above 70% or upper-second class results, and able to study at postgraduate level in English.

existing.english_requirement: You must be able to do written and verbal academic work, in English, at a postgraduate level. English is the main medium of tuition at South African universities. The Foundation states its own test as a self-check and does not publish a required IELTS or TOEFL score on this page.
application_method: Register on the Foundation's applications platform after applications open on 9 March 2027
Add three recommenders on the platform before the close
Upload certificates, transcripts, ID and passport scans and both essays
Have the three recommenders sign in to the platform and upload their English letters
Submit the complete application before 14 April 2027 23:59 GMT+2
existing.selection_notes: The Foundation looks for young leaders who aspire to leadership, reconciliation, education and entrepreneurship, and who demonstrate the combination of intellect and character. Applicants are screened in rounds: a notification by mid-July indicates whether the applicant reached Round Two, by end of July for Round Three, and by end of August whether they are invited to a Final Round interview. Final Round interviews are conducted in South Africa in October, and final-round applicants based outside South Africa are flown in for an in-person interview with the selection committee. Selected scholars are notified by the end of October.
existing.best_fit: African citizens aged 19 to 29 in the year of applying, with an undergraduate degree above 70% or an upper-second class Honours, who intend to study an Honours or Masters degree in South Africa and can commit to the compulsory leadership programme.
existing.notes: The scholarship cannot be deferred: you must accept it for the year it is offered. Attendance at the residential workshops and regional pods is mandatory and a condition of the scholarship, and the Foundation will not accept travel outside South Africa, even for research purposes, as a reason for absence. You may not hold other scholarships or funded opportunities and may not do paid work for more than 12 hours a week. The award is conditional on you being offered a place at a South African institution, and the Foundation does not apply to universities for you. If you are not accepted by a South African institution in time, you cannot accept the scholarship. The Foundation does not pay visa application costs, and states that a delayed visa may mean you cannot start on time and could lose the scholarship. Applicants from outside South Africa may need SAQA verification, which the Foundation states can take 4-8 weeks and is not covered by the award. Any amount you owe prior to becoming a Scholar is your sole responsibility. The Foundation does not fund MBAs, block courses, or courses delivered predominantly online, and distance learning is not allowed.
existing.duration: Maximum two years of funding; one year for an Honours degree, one or two years for a Masters
existing.application_period: The applications timeline runs from March to November of each year for the following year's intake. For the Class of 2028: applications open Tuesday 9 March 2027 and close 14 April 2027 23:59 GMT+2.
existing.deadline_display: Applications for 2028 will open 9 March 2027. Applications close by the end of Wednesday, 14 April 2027 23:59 GMT+2.
